porosity_frac.name: Open porosity (harmonised void area fraction) with single-image CI
porosity_frac.why: Electrolyte volume and ionic transport: D_eff ~ porosity^alpha (Bruggeman; alpha 1.5 for spheres, higher through-plane for aligned flake graphite). Trade-off, best value = match baseline. Lower = more tortuous, longer ion paths, poorer rate

si_solid_frac.name: Si-phase (bright) area fraction of solid, harmonised, with single-image CI
si_solid_frac.why: Si-phase dose sets anode capacity (N/P balance), first-cycle efficiency (SiOx irreversible silicate formation), swelling and Si-specific fade: higher = more capacity now, lower ICE, more expansion, faster fade; lower = capacity shortfall.

si_n_per_1000um2.name: Si-phase (bright) area fraction of solid, harmonised, with single-image CI
si_n_per_1000um2.why: Si-phase dose sets anode capacity (N/P balance), first-cycle efficiency (SiOx irreversible silicate formation), swelling and Si-specific fade: higher = more capacity now, lower ICE, more expansion, faster fade; lower = capacity shortfall.

si_d50_um.name: Si-phase particle size, shape, alignment, agglomeration and pore contact (harmonised BSE)
si_d50_um.why: Si particle size trades lithiation stress, fracture and contact loss (coarse) against surface area, SEI and ICE (fine); low solidity is ambiguous (dense aggregates fade fast, mesoporosity buffers stress); agglomerates are plausible local sw

porosity_block_cv.name: Spatial heterogeneity of pore and Si-phase fractions (tile CV, excess over ImageRep)
porosity_block_cv.why: Si-rich or pore-poor patches are local swelling, current-density and Li-plating hot-spots (model studies on SiO/graphite); uneven tiles point at mixing/dispersion, binder migration or uneven calendering. Counter-evidence: active-material cl

thin_solid_frac.name: Thin-solid fraction (ligaments, flake tips and slivers thinner than 0.3-0.8 um)
thin_solid_frac.why: Thin ligaments are fine fragments and exposed graphite edges: more edge-plane surface in contact with electrolyte means more SEI formation and first-cycle (irreversible) capacity loss, and fragmented, weakly connected particles.

depth_porosity_b0_frac.name: Depth profiles (porosity, carbon-binder, bright phase vs coating depth)
depth_porosity_b0_frac.why: Fast drying makes binder migrate to the top surface, leaving the current-collector interface binder-poor - weak adhesion and delamination during cycling. Exactly the "fine now, worse later" defect.

cc_interface_horiz_share_bottom_frac.name: Horizontal pores at the current-collector interface (delamination / adhesion indicator)
cc_interface_horiz_share_bottom_frac.why: Coating/current-collector debonding shows as long horizontal gaps parallel to the foil in cross-section; poor adhesion raises contact resistance and lets the coating delaminate on cycling or calendering.

local_porosity_q25_frac.name: Local porosity distribution: dense, pore-starved patches
local_porosity_q25_frac.why: Active material in pore-starved patches is reached only through long solid paths: higher local ionic resistance, lagging lithiation and Li plating at fast charge; uneven calendering or mixing produces such patches.

local_porosity_dense_window_frac.name: Local porosity distribution: dense, pore-starved patches
local_porosity_dense_window_frac.why: Active material in pore-starved patches is reached only through long solid paths: higher local ionic resistance, lagging lithiation and Li plating at fast charge; uneven calendering or mixing produces such patches.

si_depth_b0_solid_frac.name: Si share of the solid and Si particle size vs depth from the current collector
si_depth_b0_solid_frac.why: Sedimentation-dominated drying piles settling particles up near the current collector; Stokes speed goes with density contrast x size^2, and Si/SiOx is barely denser than graphite, so a Si gradient would mostly mean coarse Si or agglomerate
